# A four-fiber monotone obstruction to the single-middle payment

Let d=20, T be the standard d-simplex, V=|T|, and
Gamma=(20/21)^20. Consider the actual common-vertex fibers

    K_k=r_k T,  (r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3)=(94,97,100,103)/100.    (1)

The radii are positive and affine on the entire base interval [0,3].
Consequently C={(z,x):0<=z<=3, x in (94+3z)T/100} is a full
convex body, is the convex hull of its integer fibers, and has exactly
the four positive integer fibers (1). Set M=V sum_k r_k^20.

The proposed single-middle subset payment is

    L=Gamma+lambda_20 (97/100)^20,

in units of V. Even when combined with the heaviest ordinary own-fiber
payment Gamma(103/100)^20, it does not reach Gamma M/(2V):

    max{L, Gamma(103/100)^20}< (Gamma/2)sum_k r_k^20.     (2)

This is a failure of these specified lower certificates, not a depth
counterexample. Section 2 gives an explicit actual center that exceeds
the intended target.

## 1. Exact rational certificate

The sharp weighted-tail theorem proves lambda_d<=4 Gamma_d^2; see
`candidate bb74919333cc624f`, Section 1.
It therefore suffices for the first inequality in (2) to verify

    21^20(94^20+97^20-100^20+103^20)
       -8*20^20*97^20 >0.

The integer on the left is exactly

    1137549378322964594658090728038214421874179602838935201279638978.

For the second inequality in (2), the exact positive integer is

    94^20+97^20+100^20-103^20
      =277893493887952690657232019960683602976.

For orientation only, the target divided by V is approximately
0.6859410860, the rational upper bound on L is approximately
0.6858640368, and the heavy own-fiber payment is approximately
0.6807043292. The two strict inequalities are established by the
displayed integers, not these decimal values.

## 2. An actual safe center

The fiber-centroid path r_k g_T is affine. Use the point

    y=(2,g_T).

For any nonvertical ambient halfspace through y, its value at the four
fiber centroids is an affine scalar function of k vanishing at k=2.
Thus the halfspace contains the centroids of either all k<=2 or all
k>=2. In each such fiber ordinary Grunbaum contributes at least
Gamma times its volume. Both closed tails have mass exceeding M/2:

    r_0^20+r_1^20+1 > r_3^20,
    1+r_3^20 > r_0^20+r_1^20.

The first is the second exact integer above; the second follows term
by term from 1>r_0^20 and r_3^20>r_1^20. The same closed-tail bound
holds directly for vertical halfspaces. Therefore the actual absolute
depth at y is strictly larger than Gamma M/2.

No conclusion about failure of any actual centroid selector, the
sharp mixed depth bound, or a coupled four-fiber method follows from
(2). The example only rules out completing the monotone case by this
single-middle payment plus the heaviest own-fiber payment.

The companion exact verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_four_simplex_ordered_peak_and_monotone_gap.py`.
